content.title: Howard Men’s and Women’s Basketball Sweep MEAC Titles for First Time Since 1992
content.text: The Howard men women MEAC championship sweep is official after both Bison basketball programs captured conference titles, marking the first time since 1992 that Howard University has won both the men’s and women’s Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference championships in the same season. The historic milestone came during the 2026 MEAC Basketball Tournament at the Norfolk Scope Arena, where the Bison delivered two championship performances that sent both teams to the NCAA Tournament. With the victories, Howard University secured automatic bids to the NCAA Division I Men’s Basketball Tournament and the NCAA Division I Women’s Basketball Tournament, giving the Bison an opportunity to represent the Mid‑Eastern Athletic Conference on the national stage. The Howard men women MEAC championship sweep highlights one of the most successful seasons in recent program history and reconnects the Bison to a rare achievement last reached more than three decades ago. Howard men claim MEAC title and March Madness berth Howard’s men’s basketball team secured its place in March Madness after defeating North Carolina Central University in the MEAC championship game. The victory delivered the conference’s automatic NCAA Tournament bid and continued the Bison’s strong run within the MEAC over the past several seasons. Howard has emerged as one of the conference’s most consistent programs, frequently appearing in the MEAC championship game and establishing itself as a top contender in the league. For the players and coaching staff, the win represents the culmination of a season built on defensive discipline, balanced scoring, and the ability to execute in high-pressure tournament moments. The Howard men women MEAC championship sweep ensures the Bison will again represent HBCU basketball on college basketball’s biggest stage. Howard women dominate MEAC tournament run Howard’s women’s basketball program also delivered a strong performance throughout the conference tournament to claim the MEAC championship. The Bison women advanced through the tournament with a combination of defensive intensity and efficient offense, ultimately capturing the conference title and securing their ticket to the NCAA Tournament. Winning the championship gives the program the opportunity to compete in the national tournament and showcase its talent on one of the biggest stages in women’s college basketball. The Howard men women MEAC championship achievement demonstrates the strength of both programs and reflects the depth of talent across the Bison roster. First sweep since 1992 The dual conference championships mark a historic moment for Howard athletics. The last time both the men’s and women’s teams captured MEAC titles in the same season was 1992, making the 2026 sweep the first time the accomplishment has been achieved in more than 30 years. Moments like this are rare in collegiate athletics, particularly within the same program and conference tournament. The Howard men women MEAC championship sweep reinforces the university’s continued commitment to athletic excellence and highlights the growth of both basketball programs. Howard’s success also brings attention to the broader impact of HBCU basketball programs across the NCAA landscape. Historically Black colleges and universities have long produced elite basketball talent, and conference championships like these help elevate the visibility of those programs nationally. The MEAC continues to serve as a platform for HBCU programs to compete for NCAA Tournament bids while showcasing the energy and culture that make HBCU athletics unique. With both the men’s and women’s teams now headed to their respective NCAA tournaments, Howard will represent not only its university but also the pride of the HBCU community. Bison prepare for the NCAA Tournament With the Howard men women MEAC championship sweep complete, the focus now shifts to the NCAA Tournament brackets. Both teams will learn their tournament opponents during Selection Sunday, when the full fields for the men’s and women’s tournaments are announced. For the Bison, the opportunity represents a chance to build on the historic season and potentially deliver another memorable moment on the national stage. Whether facing higher-seeded opponents or competing in early-round matchups, Howard will enter the tournament carrying the momentum of a historic conference sweep.
